category.title: Advanced Strings & Automata
category.description: Trie, Suffix Array, LCP Array (Kasai), Suffix Tree (Ukkonen), Suffix Automaton (SAM), Aho-Corasick, Boyer-Moore, KMP, Z-Algorithm, Rabin-Karp, Manacher's Algorithm & Applications.

algorithms.title: Trie (Prefix Tree) Foundations
algorithms.summary: Tree-based data structure used to store a dynamic set of strings where keys are usually strings. Allows rapid O(L) prefix lookup and autocomplete.
explanation: 1. Each node represents a character transition in an alphabet.
2. Root represents an empty string.
3. Path from root to a node forms a prefix.
4. `isEndOfWord` flag marks complete string terminals.

exampleTrace.title: Insert 'cat', 'car', search 'car', startsWith 'ca'
traceSteps: Search 'car': Traverse root->c->a->r. node.isEnd == true -> return True.
startsWith 'ca': Traverse root->c->a. Node exists -> return True.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Provides fast O(L) retrieval of strings with a common prefix.
wAnswers.whenToUse: Autocomplete systems, dictionary lookups, spell checkers, prefix matching.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Search engines, routers (IP routing tables), text editors.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Lookup time depends only on string length L, not the total number of dictionary words N.

algorithms.title: Suffix Array Construction
algorithms.timeComplexity: O(N log N) or O(N log^2 N)
algorithms.summary: A sorted array of all suffixes of a string. Provides compact O(N) space memory layout for substring pattern matching and string analysis.
explanation: 1. Suffix array `SA[i]` stores the starting index of the i-th lexicographically smallest suffix.
2. Built iteratively using Prefix Doubling: sort suffixes by first k=1, 2, 4, 8... characters.
3. Uses rank equivalence pairs `(rank[i], rank[i + k])` to update ranks at each step.
4. Achieves O(N log N) using counting sort or O(N log^2 N) using standard sorting.

exampleTrace.title: Build Suffix Array for string S = 'banana$'

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Sorts all suffixes of a string lexicographically in compact array form.
wAnswers.whenToUse: Pattern searching in genome sequences, string matching, LCP calculation.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Bioinformatics (DNA sequence analysis), text search engines.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Uses only O(N) space compared to O(N^2) for explicit suffix trees.

codeTemplates.code:
def build_suffix_array(s: str) -> list[int]:
    s += '$'
    n = len(s)
    sa = list(range(n))
    rank = [ord(c) for c in s]
    tmp = [0] * n
    k = 1
    while k < n:
        sa.sort(key=lambda i: (rank[i], rank[i + k] if i + k < n else -1))
        tmp[sa[0]] = 0
        for i in range(1, n):
            prev, curr = sa[i - 1], sa[i]
            p_pair = (rank[prev], rank[prev + k] if prev + k < n else -1)
            c_pair = (rank[curr], rank[curr + k] if curr + k < n else -1)
            tmp[curr] = tmp[prev] + (1 if p_pair != c_pair else 0)
        rank = tmp[:]
        if rank[sa[-1]] == n - 1:
            break
        k *= 2
    return sa

algorithms.title: LCP Array (Kasai's Algorithm)
algorithms.summary: Computes the Longest Common Prefix (LCP) between adjacent suffixes in the sorted Suffix Array in linear O(N) time using Kasai's property.
explanation: 1. Kasai's Key Insight: LCP of suffix starting at `i` is at least `LCP(suffix(i-1)) - 1`.
2. Maintain inverse Suffix Array `rank[sa[i]] = i`.
3. Iterate through original string index `i` from 0 to N-1.
4. Compare suffix starting at `i` with suffix starting at `sa[rank[i] - 1]`.

exampleTrace.title: Kasai LCP Trace for S = 'banana$', SA = [6, 5, 3, 1, 0, 4, 2]
traceSteps: Kasai computes all adjacent LCP values in a single O(N) sweep!

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Calculates longest common prefix of adjacent suffixes in linear time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: Finding distinct substrings, longest repeated substrings, pattern counting.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Full-text search indexing, sequence alignment algorithms.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Avoids naive O(N^2) character comparisons by reusing match lengths.

algorithms.title: Suffix Tree & Ukkonen's Algorithm
algorithms.summary: Compressed trie containing all suffixes of a text. Ukkonen's algorithm builds it in online linear time O(N) using active point & suffix link transitions.
explanation: 1. Suffix Tree represents all N suffixes in a compressed tree with O(N) nodes.
2. Ukkonen's Online Algorithm processes characters one by one from left to right.
3. Active Point `(activeNode, activeEdge, activeLength)` tracks current insertion location.
4. Suffix Links allow instant jumping to process remaining suffixes after node splitting.

exampleTrace.title: Ukkonen Build Step for 'abcab$'
traceSteps: Step 2: Add 'a'. Character 'a' already exists on edge from root. Increment activeLength.
Step 3: Add 'b'. Character 'b' matches active edge.
Step 4: Add '$'. Match fails, split edge, create new internal node, follow suffix link to process remaining suffixes.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Solves complex string queries (substring search, matching, palindromes) in optimal linear time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When querying multiple patterns against a fixed text or finding complex repeating structures.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Genomics tools (BLAST), text data compression (BWT), full-text search.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Provides O(M) pattern lookup independent of text length N.

algorithms.title: Suffix Automaton (SAM / DAWG)
algorithms.summary: Direct Acyclic Word Graph (DAWG) that encapsulates all substrings of a string in a minimal deterministic finite automaton with O(N) states and transitions.
explanation: 1. State: Equivalency class of substrings having the exact same set of end positions (`endpos`).
2. Transitions: Directed edges labeled with characters representing string extension.
3. Suffix Link (`link`): Points to state representing the longest proper suffix with a larger `endpos` set.
4. Online O(N) Construction: Appends characters one by one, adding at most 2 states per step.

exampleTrace.title: Build SAM for S = 'aba'
traceSteps: Add 'b': Create State 2 (len=2, link=0, trans['b']=2 from st 1)
Add 'a': Create State 3 (len=3, link=1, trans['a']=3 from st 2)
SAM encodes all 5 substrings {'a', 'b', 'ab', 'ba', 'aba'} in 4 states!

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Encodes all substrings of a text into a minimal state automaton.
wAnswers.whenToUse: Counting distinct substrings, finding longest common substring, occurrence counting.
wAnswers.whereUsed: High-performance string matching engines, bioinformatics, automated translation.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Stronger and faster than Suffix Tree with smaller constant factor and simpler online transitions.

algorithms.title: Application: Distinct Substrings Count
algorithms.summary: Computes total number of distinct non-empty substrings of a string S using either Suffix Array + LCP Array or Suffix Automaton.
explanation: 1. Total substrings of length N = N * (N + 1) / 2.
2. Duplicate substrings correspond exactly to LCP values between adjacent sorted suffixes.
3. Formula 1 (Suffix Array): `Distinct Count = N * (N + 1) / 2 - Sum(LCP[i])`.
4. Formula 2 (SAM): `Distinct Count = Sum(st[i].len - st[i].link)` for all states i > 0.

exampleTrace.title: Count distinct substrings of 'azaba'
traceSteps: String length N = 5. Total possible substrings = 5 * 6 / 2 = 15.
LCP values for sorted suffixes = [0, 0, 1, 0, 1]. Sum(LCP) = 2.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Counts unique non-empty substrings without explicit set hashing.
wAnswers.whenToUse: Combinatorial string problems, string entropy analysis.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Computes exact count in O(N) time compared to naive O(N^2) set insertion.

algorithms.title: Application: Longest Repeated Substring
algorithms.summary: Finds the longest substring that appears at least twice in a text. Solved by finding max element in LCP array or using Suffix Automaton.
explanation: 1. A repeated substring appears as a common prefix of two distinct suffixes.
2. The length of the longest repeated substring is equal to `max(LCP[i])` across all i.
3. Extract substring of length `max_lcp` starting at `SA[max_index]`.
4. Handles overlapping and non-overlapping substring conditions.

exampleTrace.title: Longest Repeated Substring in 'banana'
traceSteps: Max LCP = 3 at index of 'ana' vs 'anana'

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Identifies the longest substring with multiple occurrences.
wAnswers.whenToUse: Data compression (LZ77/LZ78), DNA tandem repeat identification.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(N) linear time search using precomputed LCP array.

algorithms.title: Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) & Prefix Function
algorithms.summary: Fast pattern matching using the Prefix Function (pi array / LPS array) to skip unnecessary character comparisons when mismatch occurs.
explanation: 1. Precomputes `pi[i]`: length of the longest proper prefix of `pattern[0...i]` that is also a suffix of `pattern[0...i]`.
2. When a mismatch occurs at text index `i` and pattern index `j`, shift pattern by setting `j = pi[j - 1]` instead of rewinding text.
3. Guarantees linear O(N + M) worst-case time complexity.

exampleTrace.title: KMP search for Pattern 'ababa' in Text 'ababcaba'
traceSteps: Matching text 'ababc...': mismatch at 'c' vs pattern[4]='a'.
Fallback: j = pi[3] = 2. Resume comparing from pattern index 2 without resetting text pointer!

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Sub-quadratic exact pattern matching with zero back-tracking on text stream.
wAnswers.whenToUse: Text searching, string periodicities, border computations.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Grep utilities, text editor search commands, packet inspection.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Ensures O(N) text scanning by eliminating re-reading of matched characters.

algorithms.title: Z-Algorithm & Z-Array Construction
algorithms.summary: Computes Z-array where Z[i] is the length of the longest common prefix between S and the suffix of S starting at i.
explanation: 1. Maintain a Z-box `[L, R]` representing the rightmost substring matching a prefix of S.
2. For index `i`: if `i <= R`, reuse precomputed values `Z[i] = min(R - i + 1, Z[i - L])`.
3. Expand linearly past R while characters match, then update `[L, R]`.
4. Concatenate `Pattern + '$' + Text` to solve pattern matching in linear time.

exampleTrace.title: Z-array for S = 'aabxaab'
traceSteps: Z-box jumps efficiently without quadratic rescans.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Computes prefix match lengths for all suffixes of a string in O(N).
wAnswers.whenToUse: Pattern matching, period finding, string compression.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Cleaner and easier to implement than KMP while achieving identical O(N) performance.

algorithms.title: Rabin-Karp Rolling Hash Algorithm
algorithms.timeComplexity: O(N + M) average, O(N * M) worst-case without double hash
algorithms.summary: Uses polynomial rolling hash to compare pattern hash with sliding window text hashes in O(1) time per window shift.
explanation: 1. Hash formula: `H = (c1 * p^(m-1) + c2 * p^(m-2) + ... + cm) % MOD`.
2. Rolling Hash update when sliding window from `[i..i+m-1]` to `[i+1..i+m]`:
`H_new = (H_old - text[i] * p^(m-1)) * p + text[i+m] % MOD`.
3. Double hashing minimizes collision probability to negligible levels.

exampleTrace.title: Rabin-Karp search for pattern 'abc' in 'abxabc'
traceSteps: Window 3 'abc': Hash = 1057 (Match! Verify string characters -> Match found at index 3)

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Multi-pattern & single-pattern matching using fast hash comparisons.
wAnswers.whenToUse: Plagiarism detection, multi-pattern matching, 2D grid pattern search.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(1) window update constant factor speedup.

algorithms.title: Aho-Corasick Automaton
algorithms.summary: Multi-pattern string matching dictionary automaton that combines Trie structure with BFS suffix fail links (similar to KMP).
explanation: 1. Build a Trie for dictionary of patterns `P1, P2, ..., Pk`.
2. Construct Failure Links via BFS: `fail[u]` points to longest proper suffix of string at node u that is also present in Trie.
3. Process text in single pass O(N): follow transitions or fail links to collect matched pattern outputs.
4. Finds ALL occurrences of ALL dictionary patterns simultaneously in linear time!

exampleTrace.title: Aho-Corasick with Patterns ['he', 'she', 'his', 'hers'] in Text 'ushers'
traceSteps: 1. Build Trie with root -> h, s.
2. BFS computes fail links: node 'sh' fail -> 'h', node 'she' fail -> 'he'.
3. Stream text 'ushers': matches 'she' and 'he' at position 4, matches 'hers' at position 5.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Simultaneous multi-pattern exact keyword searching in text.
wAnswers.whenToUse: Antivirus virus signature scanners, network intrusion detection systems (NIDS), profanity filters.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Snort NIDS, clamav antivirus engines, web application firewalls.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Processes text character-by-character in O(N) independent of dictionary size!

algorithms.title: Boyer-Moore String Search Algorithm
algorithms.timeComplexity: O(N / M) best/average, O(N * M) worst without Good Suffix heuristic
algorithms.summary: Extremely fast single-pattern matching algorithm that compares characters right-to-left and uses Bad Character & Good Suffix shift rules to skip alignment blocks.
explanation: 1. Right-to-Left Comparison: Starts comparing pattern from rightmost character `pattern[m-1]` back to `pattern[0]`.
2. Bad Character Rule: Shifts pattern so mismatched text character aligns with its rightmost occurrence in pattern.
3. Good Suffix Rule: Shifts pattern so matched suffix aligns with another matching substring in pattern.
4. Maximum Shift: Advances alignment by `max(bad_char_shift, good_suffix_shift)`, jumping ahead by up to M characters at a time.

exampleTrace.title: Boyer-Moore Search for Pattern 'NEEDLE' in Text 'FINDINAHAYSTACKNEEDLE'
traceSteps: Compare pattern[5]='E' with text char at index 5 'I'.
Bad char 'I' does not exist in 'NEEDLE' -> Shift entire pattern by 6 positions!
Skips 6 text characters in a single comparison step!

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Sub-linear average-case pattern matching for large alphabets.
wAnswers.whenToUse: Searching long natural language text files or large documents.
wAnswers.whereUsed: GNU grep, text editor Ctrl+F search algorithms.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Averages O(N/M) runtime because it skips text characters without inspecting them.

algorithms.title: Manacher's Algorithm (Palindrome Radii)
algorithms.summary: Finds all palindrome radii and the longest palindromic substring in linear O(N) time by transforming the string with boundary delimiters and maintaining a palindrome center-right boundary.
explanation: 1. Preprocessing: Insert `#` between characters (`baba` -> `#b#a#b#a#`) to unify even and odd palindrome handling.
2. Maintain center `C` and rightmost boundary `R` of the longest palindrome discovered so far.
3. Mirror Property: For index `i`, its mirror is `i_mirror = 2*C - i`. If `i < R`, initialize `P[i] = min(R - i, P[i_mirror])`.
4. Expand palindrome radius `P[i]` beyond `R` as long as matching characters extend.
5. Update `C` and `R` whenever `i + P[i] > R`.

exampleTrace.title: Manacher's Trace on 'babad'
traceSteps: Max radius = 3 at center 'a'. Extracted longest palindromic substring = 'bab' (or 'aba').

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Computes all palindrome radii and finds longest palindromic substring in optimal linear time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: Palindromic substring analysis, string symmetry queries.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Bioinformatics DNA hairpins detection, text analysis algorithms.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Replaces naive O(N^2) center expansion with optimal linear O(N) time.
